items: Replica migration: a master with spare replicas donates one
It goes to an orphaned master automatically
Governed by `cluster-migration-barrier`

blocks.title: Minority Partition
blocks.text: Masters that cannot reach a majority stop accepting writes. That limits split-brain; it does not eliminate it.

blocks.title: Write Loss Window
blocks.text: Replication is async. Writes acked by the old master but not yet shipped are simply gone after promotion.
A separate process that monitors a master/replica set, elects a new master when the old one dies, and tells clients where to go.

items: Deploy an odd number, at least 3
Put them on separate failure domains
Quorum = how many must agree the master is down

blocks.title: Two Different Majorities
blocks.text: Quorum authorizes the verdict. A MAJORITY of all Sentinels must then elect the leader that performs the failover.

blocks.q: Quorum 2 with 5 Sentinels — how many must be alive?
a_bullets: But 3 of 5 must be alive to elect a leader
Low quorum speeds detection, never sizing

items: Raft-like term and vote, one per failover epoch
Only the elected leader performs the promotion
Losing Sentinels stand down and observe
Best replica: by priority, then offset, then run-id
`replica-priority 0` = never promotable
Use 0 for a backup or analytics node
Replicas found via the master's `INFO` output
Other Sentinels found on `__sentinel__:hello` pub/sub
Sentinel rewrites its own config file on state change
Never hand-edit a running Sentinel's config

blocks.title: parallel-syncs
items: Caps how many replicas resync at once
High: fast recovery, heavy master load
1: slow rollout, gentle on the new master

blocks.title: Sentinel Does Not Shard
blocks.text: One dataset, one master. Sentinel and Cluster are alternatives — Cluster has its own failover and never uses Sentinel.
The master replies OK before the replica has the write. That reply is a prediction, not a durability guarantee.

items: `WAIT` improves the odds; it is not a commit protocol
`min-replicas-max-lag` refuses writes when replicas lag
`WAITAOF` is disk durability, not agreement
Nothing here makes Redis a consensus store

blocks.title: Split-Brain Window
blocks.text: An isolated master keeps accepting writes for up to `cluster-node-timeout` before it notices and stops. Those writes are on the losing side.

blocks.title: Locking
blocks.text: Redlock and Redis distributed locks are contested. Never assume a lock survives a failover.

items: Assuming MULTI spans shards — it is rejected, not split
Running `KEYS` or `FLUSHDB` on one node, believing you hit the cluster
A hash tag of cardinality 1, giving one giant hot slot
Pointing a non-cluster-aware client at a cluster

blocks.text: That last one surfaces MOVED errors as raw application exceptions, usually at 2 a.m. during the first reshard.

blocks.title: Big Keys
items: A multi-GB hash blocks MIGRATE
Replica full-sync becomes brutal
Shard the value, not only the keyspace

blocks.title: Operational Rule
blocks.text: Test failover on purpose, on a schedule, in daylight — before it happens to you at 3 a.m. for the first time.

items: 16384 hash slots; `slot = CRC16(key) mod 16384`
Hash tag `{...}` overrides what gets hashed
Each master owns a set of slots
All 16384 covered, or writes refuse (default)
The slot bitmap rides in every gossip heartbeat
16384 bits = 2 KB per packet; 65536 = 8 KB
Redis targets roughly 1000 nodes maximum

blocks.title: Check Before You Ship
blocks.text: `CLUSTER KEYSLOT 'user:{1000}:profile'` must equal `CLUSTER KEYSLOT '{1000}'`. If it does not, your tag is silently broken.
Multi-key rule: same slot or rejected. Hash tags are the only sanctioned workaround, and they are a schema decision.

items: Most smart clients fan out for you — verify yours does
`SCAN`, `KEYS`, `DBSIZE` are all per-node
No `SELECT`: cluster mode has database 0 only
7.0 sharded pub/sub: `SSUBSCRIBE` stays on one shard

blocks.title: Reshard Safety
items: MIGRATE blocks both nodes per batch
Keep batch sizes small
Reshard slots away BEFORE del-node
`--cluster fix` clears stuck slots

blocks.title: Two Quorums To Keep Straight
blocks.text: Cluster votes among masters. Sentinel votes among Sentinels. Mixing the two mental models is how sizing goes wrong.

slides.page_title: Summary: The Whole Model on One Page

items: Gossip runs on the client port + 10000
PFAIL: one node missed `cluster-node-timeout`
FAIL: a majority of masters agree, then broadcast
Only masters vote; replicas gossip but do not count
Cluster: 3 masters + 3 replicas minimum
Sentinel: 3 minimum, odd, on separate hosts
Never co-locate all quorum members on one rack

a_bullets: Failure detection needs a majority of masters
2 masters cannot form a majority after one dies
3 masters alone still have no failover target

blocks.title: Key Config Dials
items: `cluster-node-timeout`
`cluster-require-full-coverage`
`cluster-migration-barrier`
`down-after-milliseconds`, quorum, `replica-priority`

blocks.title: Consistency Ceiling
blocks.text: Async replication means a bounded window of acknowledged-but-lost writes. `WAIT` narrows the window; nothing removes it.

blocks.title: Read Scaling
blocks.text: `READONLY` on a replica connection serves reads there instead of redirecting. `READWRITE` reverts it. Those reads may be stale.

blocks.title: Pre-Launch Checklist
items: Cluster-aware client verified (ASK too)
Hash tags designed, cardinality checked
No big keys; monitoring per node
Failover drill actually run

caption.text: Part 2 of REDIS CLUSTER & SENTINEL. 16384. Not 65536, not a consistent-hashing ring — because the slot bitmap rides inside every gossip heartbeat, and 2 KB per packet beats 8 KB. That single design choice explains MOVED, ASK, CROSSSLOT, and why a hash tag of `{prod}` will haunt you forever. Ten pages on how Redis Cluster really shards, reshards and fails over, plus where Sentinel fits and where it does not.
